name: Finance
navDesc: What banking and fintech apps rely on, and where the openings are.

hero.headline: Your users open the app once. Then the habit never forms.
hero.sub: Banking, investing, and budgeting apps win on engagement, not features. We study how the most habit-forming apps keep people coming back, and help your team apply what fits your product — without turning people's money into a game.

problems.title: The one-and-done signup
problems.body: People link an account, check a balance, and never build a reason to come back. Activation looks fine; the second week falls off a cliff.

problems.title: Saving feels like a chore
problems.body: The behaviours you want — saving, budgeting, investing on a schedule — carry no momentum, so good intentions stall within days.

problems.title: Nothing to return for
problems.body: Between the monthly statement and the next bill, there is no reason to open the app. Engagement collapses to a utility people tolerate.

problems.title: Engagement that feels gimmicky
problems.body: Bolt-on points and badges read as childish next to someone's salary, and they quietly erode the trust a finance brand depends on.

problems.title: Progress no one can see
problems.body: Users can't watch themselves improving, so the early effort never compounds into the kind of loyalty that survives a competitor's ad.

problems.title: Features ship, retention doesn't move
problems.body: You keep adding tools, but the number that matters — who is still here in ninety days — refuses to move. The roadmap is busy and the curve is flat.

report.title: Gamification in Finance
report.body: What banking and fintech apps rely on for engagement and retention — app by app, mechanic by mechanic — and where the openings are for products that haven't caught up yet. Enter your email and we'll send you the full report.
